stories.title: Which LA candidates Airbnb has backed, LA mayoral candidates talk to voters, Musical honors civil rights icon Dolores Huerta — Afternoon Edition
stories.take: The answer: Airbnb has spent millions backing Mayor Karen Bass, John McKinney for city attorney, and Jose Ugarte in District 9 — and against DSA-backed Estuardo Mazariegos — because Bass wants to loosen short-term rental rules for the 2028 Olympics and the next city attorney inherits the Airbnb price-gouging lawsuit • Final pitches: Bass voted in Koreatown as the progress candidate; Raman campaigned in Northridge as the anti-establishment choice; polls are open Tuesday 7am-8pm • The touring musical 'Si Se Puede' honors the late Dolores Huerta and the women of the farmworker movement; next free LA show is Wednesday, November 4

stories.title: Economy of Scale: New Finance (Sponsored Content)
stories.take: Sponsored Dubai episode on scaling fintech: VARA, the first dedicated virtual-asset regulator, has gone from 14 to 57 licensed firms on a principles-based rulebook with heavy firm engagement • Ripple has expanded from XRP payments into its RLUSD stablecoin, custody and prime brokerage, doubling Dubai headcount, with Middle East-Africa corridor growth of 40-50% a year • Tokenization has shifted from speculation to rails: about $50B under management versus $1.5B in early 2023, Dubai land titles going on chain, and tokenized money-market funds used as repo collateral named the next wave

stories.title: Does Democrats’ Future Lie With Moderates or Progressives?
stories.take: The answer: no single race decides it — watch Michigan, where El-Sayed raised $2.4M in a day after Stevens endorsed his Republican opponent; Maine, where progressive Troy Jackson takes on Susan Collins; and Texas, where Talarico rejects the progressive label and runs top-versus-bottom against the billionaire class • The midterms are a referendum on Trump and Democrats are poised to retake the House, but the party's own brand has not resurged, leaving its 2028 message unsettled • Also in the show: Apple revenue grew 12% with a 47.9% gross margin, Anthropic IPO talk cooled to $1.5-1.6 trillion, and Virginia's GPS speed caps for super-speeders are showing early glitches

stories.title: Earnings Special: Apple's Forecast Disappoints, Despite Topping Estimates
stories.take: Apple beat on the top and bottom line in its first report under CEO John Ternus: revenue $114.48B vs $113.47B expected, EPS $2.10 vs $2.00, iPhone revenue $57.58B on the 18 Pro line • Greater China missed again at $17.54B vs $18.75B, iPad and wearables missed, and services met at $31.57B but is decelerating • Everything rides on December guidance and the iPhone Duo: supply is so tight that many pre-orders ship in late January; Gurman sees about 15M units this year and easier availability by February-March • Gurman: Siri AI finally works for most on-phone tasks but is no agent yet, and services is leaking Google search revenue as users move to AI apps

stories.title: Why raise money in euros?
stories.take: The answer: the US bond market is saturated with tech debt — Microsoft $25B last week, Oracle $10B this week — some investors are capped or nervous, these firms earn plenty of euros to repay in euros, and European borrowing can run more than 1.5 points cheaper; Alphabet is issuing just under $7B there and Meta may follow • Jobs Week lands in a 'low hire, low fire' market: openings weak, advertised pay growth below inflation, long-term unemployment rising • K2 Space in Torrance is building the largest satellites ever — 50-100 meter solar arrays, a roughly $7B valuation, Space Force and Golden Dome work — and argues most compute moves to orbit in 5-10 years • Anthropic says it is under contract for $895B of compute and data centers, $70B due within a year, against $33B of revenue through September

stories.title: Long-unfinished film captures a Harlem Renaissance reunion
stories.take: LA's mayoral race is tied 40-40 in the final Berkeley/LA Times poll with nearly 20% undecided — many of them former Spencer Pratt voters — as the carpenters back Raman and police and Airbnb-linked groups back Bass • The Supreme Court rejected Trump's emergency appeal on the 20,000 California ballots; Loyola's Jessica Levinson says the DOJ had no legal theory, and a UCLA study found 42% of the list is not even on the state voter rolls • The headline film: William Greaves gathered surviving Harlem Renaissance luminaries at Duke Ellington's townhouse in 1972 and never finished the movie — his son David, a cameraman that day at 26, has released it as 'Once Upon a Time in Harlem' • Plus 'Heart of Gold,' the Neil Young tribute out Friday with Edie Brickell, Jim James and King Princess, benefiting the Bridge School

stories.title: SCOTUS rejects appeal to set aside LA ballots, Airbnb and LA elections, LA's pilot program for indie films extended — Evening Edition
stories.take: The Supreme Court rejected the DOJ bid to set aside thousands of California ballots after lower courts found the 20,000-voter list unreliable; 34 people statewide have now been charged with non-citizen voting, and the green-card holders arrested last month face prison and deportation • Airbnb's millions back Bass, city attorney candidate John McKinney and council candidates Jose Ugarte and Tim Gaspar, as Bass pushes looser short-term rental rules before the 2028 Olympics • Film LA extends the low-cost permit pilot through April: 400+ permits and $400,000 saved for indie filmmakers in six months • LAUSD school-choice applications close this Friday
